title: Semantic Splitter and Fractional Deployment Regulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a policy engine that controls fractional traffic exposure using a semantic-splitting heuristic. The engine will support micro-fractions (0.01% increments), semantic cohort routing (based on request embedding similarity to user-defined slices), shadow probing, and automatic rollback based on multi-signal anomaly detection. Goal: enable safer, higher-velocity model introductions while preserving latency SLOs and minimizing customer exposure to regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine accepts declarative policies (traffic fraction, step schedule, cohort selectors, probe windows)
Able to route traffic using embedding-based cohort selectors with <2% routing error on testbench
Auto-rollback triggers when any of the configured signals breach thresholds for the configured lookback window
Shadow probing can send up to 100% mirrored traffic for selected cohorts without affecting primary latency >1%
End-to-end e2e tests and simulator (synthetic traffic) exercises step schedules and rollback behavior
Console shows per-fraction latency/cost/QoS telemetry and explains rollback reason
decisions: Use embedding-based semantic selectors (cosine similarity) rather than strict header/cohort matching to enable slice-based canaries
Fraction granularity: 0.01% for the first 1% then adaptively coarsen to 0.1% beyond 10% to reduce scheduler churn
Rollback signals: aggregate of latency p95, error rate, semantic-quality-regression score; require 2-of-3 to trigger automatic rollback in production
Probe strategy: initial probe at 0.01% for 30 minutes, then 0.1% for 2 hours before a step increase unless telemetry passes
Telemetry retention: high-resolution for probe windows (1s bins for 1 hour), aggregated thereafter

Engineering: implement multi-signal anomaly detector and rollback actuator

risks: Semantic selector may misclassify traffic slices leading to unexpected user exposure; mitigation: conservative default thresholds and allow customer-provided embeddings
High-cardinality cohorts could increase routing table size and CPU; mitigation: LRU eviction and coarsening policy
Auto-rollback false positives — could cause unnecessary rollbacks under transient spikes; mitigation: require multi-signal agreement + debounce window
Shadowing at high volume could increase cost and KV cache pressure; mitigation: rate-limit shadows and sample requests
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for selector and fraction scheduler; 2) Simulator scenarios: gradual degradation, sudden QoS regression, noisy transient spike; 3) Staging canary run against small internal cohort (0.05%) with shadowing enabled; 4) Run automated rollback scenarios and verify rollback logs and console explanations
rollout_strategy_summary: Start with semantically selected micro-probes (0.01% for 30m), escalate fractions via an adaptive schedule (doubling every success window until target fraction), maintain shadow probes for mirrors. If detector signals a breach (2 of 3 signals) sustained for debounce window (15m), automatically rollback to previous stable variant and notify on-call with detailed telemetry.
notes: PM requested the ability for customers to pin policies to Dedicated vs Hosted toggles — will scope in follow-up
Design asked to expose a simulator API so Solutions Engineers can pre-validate policies for large customers
Security: semantic selectors must not log raw request text; only hashed embeddings and selector metadata are logged
